newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet session mostly weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet session mostly weaker.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished a session of lethargic range-trading mostly weaker.
The lack of economic data, plus trepidation about next week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, kept many players glued to the sidelines.
"I've got good news: we're six minutes to the close," joked a T-bond futures floor broker near the end of a slow day's trading. "We've sat in a 10-tick range all day."
Some analysts said the long end appeared to be snagged inside a trading range until Wednesday, with a downward tilt still seen prevailing as it continues to correct downward.
Friday's close below the 113-01/32 level meant the correction had yet to run its course, said the floor broker.
"So I think it's (near term outlook) still negative," he added. "I don't think we're done (correcting) yet."
Some looked for the contract to probe next good support near 112-17/32 - 18/32 level, close to a key Gann support line and the 20-week moving average.
"They need some more energy. We need more reasons to go back up," said another broker. He noted that March T-bonds tested the upside earlier this week, stalled at 114-08/32 and since have eroded.

The market withstood the last trading day in March T-bond futures-options with little fanfare, as the contract went off the boards at midday despite the fairly large open interest that some said could have sparked a swing.
"They went off without a peep," said the second broker.
"We had a small drop to 25 (112-25/32) and couldn't get any sellers, the pit was short, we saw a couple buyers and got some shortcovering, and that was it," added the first broker.
Remarks about banking and market regulation by Fed chairman Greenspan had little impact. Nor did traders note much response to comments by Fed vice chairman Alice Rivlin.

Rivlin said there is no evidence yet that wage rises are sparking inflation because productivity appears to be growing even faster. She also said the economic risks are on the upside due to tight labor markets and that the economy is on a "good track at the moment."

March T-bonds ended down 3/32 at 112-30/32, T-notes eased 1/32 to 109-22/32, muni-bonds lost 2/32 to 117-05/32, June T-bills lost one bp to 94.94, and June Eurodollars ended flat at 94.40. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
